about: Course words: an authored word list per Arabic lesson (MyDay's own, not part of the supplied package), each word with its meaning, root, an example and a short note, beside the package's starter words (listed by id under "seed", not repeated). Fully vowelled. Each module is checked by the owner before it ships.

words.note: A greeting for anyone; a common reply is مَرْحَبًا بِكَ (to a man) or مَرْحَبًا بِكِ (to a woman).

words.example_meaning_en: Peace be upon you. — And upon you peace.
words.note: Heard everywhere in the Arab world. The reply turns it round: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. عَلَيْكُمْ is plural but is used for one person too.

words.example_meaning_en: Good morning. — Good morning (lit. morning of light).
words.note: The usual reply is صَبَاحُ النُّورِ. صَبَاح is “morning”; الْخَيْر is from the root خ-ي-ر, “good”.

words.example_meaning_en: What is your name? — My name is Sāmir.
words.note: After another word its first vowel isn't pronounced: مَا اسْمُكَ. اِسْمِي is “my name”. Plural أَسْمَاء. Classical dictionaries list it under س-م-و; Hans Wehr has it under alif.
To a woman: كَيْفَ حَالُكِ؟ The word حَال means “state, condition”.
The answer to كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟ The same for a man or a woman.

words.example_meaning_en: My name is Laylā. — Pleased to meet you!
words.note: Literally “we are honoured”. Said after names are exchanged.
Literally “with safety”: the same root as السَّلَام.

words.example_meaning_en: Good evening. — Good evening (lit. evening of light).
words.note: Like صَبَاحُ الْخَيْرِ, with the starter word مَسَاء, “evening”.

words.example_meaning_en: Sāmir is a teacher and Laylā is a student.

To a man: اِسْمَعْ.
To a woman: اِنْتَظِرِي.
It starts with أَ, a hamza that's always said. To a woman: أَغْلِقِي.
“Don't …” is لَا with a present form ending in sukūn; to a woman: لَا تَتَأَخَّرِي.
The verb after it ends in -a: أَشْرَبَ.

words.meaning_en: I can, I am able to
words.note: Followed by أَنْ and a verb.
Literally “it is necessary that”; the person is in the verb after it.
With ـكَ: “you can”; on its own: “it's possible”.
Followed by أَنْ and a verb.
The same root as مِنْ فَضْلِكَ and تَفَضَّلْ.
The same root as إِلَى اللِّقَاءِ.

words.meaning_en: what do you think? (to a man)
words.example_meaning_en: What do you think of this idea?
words.note: To a woman: مَا رَأْيُكِ؟ The word رَأْي means “opinion”.
A woman says مُوَافِقَةٌ.
The same root as آسِف, “sorry”.

words.example_meaning_en: I come to the lesson every day.
words.note: What you attend comes straight after the verb.
From the root of أَرْبَعَة, “four”: the fourth day of the week.

words.example_meaning_en: We'll meet in the morning instead of the evening.
words.note: مِنْ becomes مِنَ before the article.
Sums up what's been agreed.

words.example_meaning_en: Her book is on the desk.
words.note: ـهَا on a noun is “her”.
ة is written ت before a suffix: سَيَّارَة → سَيَّارَتُهُ.

words.meaning_en: I saw him, I saw it
words.note: ـهُ on a verb is who or what you saw: the object.
مَعَ with ـهُ: on a preposition, the suffix is who it's with.
لِ, “for”, with ـهَا. Before a suffix لِ becomes لَ (لَهُ، لَهَا، لَكَ); only لِي, “for me”, keeps the kasra.

words.example_meaning_en: This is a message from him.
words.note: مِنْ with ـهُ.

words.example_meaning_en: These are students; we know them.
words.note: ـهُمْ is “them” (men, or a mixed group).
ـنَا on a noun is “our”. On a verb it's the subject “we” (ذَهَبْنَا) or the object “us” (يَعْرِفُنَا).
Plural جُمَل.

words.example_meaning_en: سَامِرٌ is the subject in “Sāmir wrote a letter”.
words.note: A grammar word: the one who does the action.

words.example_meaning_en: Here the book is the direct object.
words.note: A grammar word: what the action is done to.
Usually shown by a ḍamma: الطَّالِبُ.
Usually shown by a fatḥa: الْكِتَابَ.

words.example_meaning_en: The noun after a preposition is genitive.
words.note: Usually shown by a kasra: فِي الْبَيْتِ.
A grammar word: “a letter (word) of pulling”, which puts the next noun in the genitive.

words.example_meaning_en: The door of the house is open.
words.note: The first noun has no article; the second makes the pair definite.
Literally “the room of sleep”.

words.meaning_en: the head of the school, head teacher
words.note: مُدِير is “manager, director”.
Plural نَوَافِذ.
A chain: the car of my-father. ـي makes it definite.

words.example_meaning_en: His house is in the centre of the town.
words.note: “In the middle of” is فِي وَسَطِ.
The same root as يَوْمُ الْجُمُعَةِ: “gathering”.

words.example_meaning_en: The head teacher's office is over there.
words.note: Three nouns in a chain: only the last has the article.

words.example_meaning_en: The teacher's new house is big.
words.note: The adjective comes after the whole chain. الْجَدِيدُ, with a ḍamma like بَيْتُ, describes the house; الْجَدِيدِ would describe the teacher.

words.example_meaning_en: There are two students in the room.
words.note: ـانِ for two, as the subject.

words.meaning_en: two houses (object, or after a preposition)
words.note: ـيْنِ for two as the object or after a preposition; ـانِ as the subject.
ة is written ت before the ending for two.

words.meaning_en: two days (object, or after a preposition)
words.example_meaning_en: I'll be back in two days.
words.note: After بَعْدَ the ending is ـيْنِ.

words.example_meaning_en: The (women) students are in the library.
words.note: A regular plural for women: ة becomes ـَات. As the object it takes kasra, not fatḥa: رَأَيْتُ الطَّالِبَاتِ.
ـِينَ after a preposition or as the object; as the subject: مُهَنْدِسُونَ.

words.example_meaning_en: The town is bigger than the village.
words.note: The same form for a feminine noun: الْمَدِينَةُ أَكْبَرُ.

words.example_meaning_en: My room is smaller than yours.
words.note: Followed by مِنْ, “than”.
The same root as كَثِيرًا, “a lot”.
The same root as قَلِيلًا, “a little”.
The same root as حَسَنًا, “all right”. أَفْضَل is also very common for “better”.

words.example_meaning_en: I live in a small village.
words.note: Plural قُرًى.
The digit is ٤ (4). With a masculine noun like قَلَم, three to ten end in ة.

words.example_meaning_en: There are seven days in a week.
words.note: The digit is ٧ (7). أَيَّام is the plural of يَوْم.

words.example_meaning_en: What is the root of this word?
words.note: Plural جُذُور.

words.example_meaning_en: The two words have the same pattern.
words.note: Also “weight”.
The فَاعِل pattern: the one who does it.

words.example_meaning_en: The name is written on the door.
words.note: The مَفْعُول pattern: what it's done to.
Plural دُرُوس. The same root as يَدْرُسُ and مَدْرَسَة.
Means the same as مُعَلِّم, which comes from another root (ع-ل-م). For a woman: مُدَرِّسَة.
The same root as مُعَلِّم and أَتَعَلَّمُ: the family shares an idea, not one meaning.

words.example_meaning_en: This book is for the school.
words.note: لِ + الْمَدْرَسَة: after لِ the article's alif isn't written.
بِ, “by, with”, + الـ + سَيَّارَة.

words.example_meaning_en: Sāmir is here, and his book is with him.
words.note: وَ + كِتَاب + هُ: three pieces in one written word.

words.example_meaning_en: The office is as big as a house.
words.note: كَـ is “like”, joined to the next word.

words.example_meaning_en: The door was closed, so I went away.
words.note: فَـ is “so, and then”, joined to the next word.
Here و is part of the root, not “and”: not every first و is the conjunction.
Here ب is part of the root, not “with”.

words.example_meaning_en: I look the word up in the dictionary.
words.note: Plural قَوَامِيس. مُعْجَم is the other common word for a dictionary.

words.example_meaning_en: The water comes out of the spring.
words.note: One word, several senses: the sentence decides which.

words.example_meaning_en: What is the plural of this word?
words.note: Dictionaries give a noun's plural beside it.

words.example_meaning_en: كِتَاب is singular, and كُتُب is plural.
words.note: The same root as مُفْرَدَات, “vocabulary”.
Plural حُرُوف. Also “small word” in grammar, as in حَرْفُ جَرٍّ.
A four-letter root. الْآلِيَّة is “automatic, by machine”.
Keep the sentence around a word before you choose its sense.
The فَاعِل pattern of قَرَأَ: the one who reads.
The مَفْعُول pattern: what can be read. الْخَطّ is “handwriting”.

words.example_meaning_en: I prefer studying in the evening.
words.note: A verbal noun: the action of يَدْرُسُ.

words.example_meaning_en: Going to work by bus is easy.
words.note: A verbal noun: the action of يَذْهَبُ.

words.example_meaning_en: My brother is a good player.
words.note: The فَاعِل pattern of لَعِبَ, “he played”.
The مَفْعُول pattern of عَرَفَ, “he knew”.
The فَاعِل pattern of سَكَنَ, “he lived (somewhere)”.
A verbal noun: the action of يَكْتُبُ.
A grammar word: a noun naming the action, like دِرَاسَة or كِتَابَة. Also “source”; plural مَصَادِر.
A plural; one word is مُفْرَدَة.

words.meaning_en: I memorise, I learn by heart
words.example_meaning_en: I learn five words by heart every day.
words.note: With a feminine noun like كَلِمَة, three to ten have no ة: خَمْسُ كَلِمَاتٍ.
What you remember comes straight after the verb.
بِسُرْعَةٍ is “quickly”.

words.example_meaning_en: I write the word on a card.
words.note: Plural بِطَاقَات.
Listen to the voice beside a word to check it.
From يَوْم, “day”.
Plural رِحْلَات.
The same root as زُرْتُ, “I visited”.

words.example_meaning_en: The return is in the evening.
words.note: The same root as عُدْتُ, “I came back”.
The same root as مُعَلِّم. جَيِّدًا here is “well, carefully”.
Plural مُلَاحَظَات.

words.example_meaning_en: I visit my mother on Saturday.
words.note: “On Saturday” is يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ.
From the root of أَحَد, “one”: the first day of the week.
From the root of خَمْسَة, “five”: the fifth day of the week.

words.example_meaning_en: I read the notice on the door.
words.note: Plural إِعْلَانَات. On notices you'll see تَفْتَحُ, “it opens”, and تُغْلِقُ, “it closes” (these forms are for a feminine noun like الْمَكْتَبَة).
Also “recording”.
Plural دَوْرَات.
Plural مَشَاكِل.
Plural حُلُول.
To a woman: يُنَاسِبُكِ.
The same root as يُمْكِنُ.

words.example_meaning_en: The hotel is near the station.
words.note: Plural فَنَادِق. A four-letter root.

words.example_meaning_en: I'd like to book a room.
words.note: Literally “I want the booking of a room”.
Plural فِقْرَات.
Plural أَسْبَاب.
Plural نَتَائِج.

words.example_meaning_en: I was late because I was busy.
words.note: لِأَنَّ, “because”, with ـنِي, “me”. The shorter لِأَنِّي is also common.

words.example_meaning_en: I like fruit, apples for example.
words.note: الْفَاكِهَة is “fruit”.

words.example_meaning_en: I check over what I wrote.
words.note: The same root as مُرَاجَعَة, “revision”.

words.example_meaning_en: I have an interest in history.
words.note: “Interested in” is مُهْتَمٌّ بِـ.
Also “date”: مَا تَارِيخُ الْيَوْمِ؟ is “what's the date today?”.
“My level” is مُسْتَوَايَ.

words.example_meaning_en: Sometimes I listen to the news.
words.note: الْأَخْبَار is “the news”.
Plural خُطُوَات.
Form II, with the middle root letter doubled. “He offers” is يُقَدِّمُ.

words.example_meaning_en: My sister helped me with the lesson.
words.note: Form III, with a long ā after the first root letter. “Help” is مُسَاعَدَة.

words.example_meaning_en: I sent a message to my friend.
words.note: Form IV begins with أَ. “He sends” is يُرْسِلُ.

words.example_meaning_en: The weather changed in the afternoon.
words.note: Form V: تَـ before form II. “He changed (something)” is غَيَّرَ.

words.example_meaning_en: The students worked together on the project.
words.note: Form VI often means doing something together. “Cooperation” is تَعَاوُن.
Form VII: it happens to the thing, with no doer named. “He broke (something)” is كَسَرَ.

words.example_meaning_en: We gathered at my grandfather’s house.
words.note: Form VIII adds ت after the first root letter. “A meeting” is اِجْتِمَاع.

words.example_meaning_en: I use the dictionary every day.
words.note: Form X begins with اِسْتَـ. Form I, خَدَمَ, is “he served”.
Hollow: the middle root letter is و. “He says” is يَقُولُ.

words.example_meaning_en: I lived in Cairo for two years.
words.note: Hollow, with ي in the middle: “he lives” is يَعِيشُ. In عِشْتُ the long ā is gone.

words.example_meaning_en: Don’t be afraid, the dog is small.
words.note: “He is afraid” is يَخَافُ. In تَخَفْ, after لَا, the long ā is gone.
Final-weak: the last root letter is و, written here as alif. “He invites” is يَدْعُو.
Final-weak with ي, written ى at the end. “He throws” is يَرْمِي.

words.example_meaning_en: He didn’t walk to work today.
words.note: “He walks” is يَمْشِي. After لَمْ the final ي goes, as in the example.

words.example_meaning_en: I stayed at home on Saturday.
words.note: “He stays” is يَبْقَى.

words.example_meaning_en: The bus stopped in front of the station.
words.note: Initial-weak: “he stands” is يَقِفُ, without the و.

words.example_meaning_en: I put the book on the desk.
words.note: “He puts” is يَضَعُ. The noun وَضْع is “situation”.

words.example_meaning_en: I replied to his message yesterday.
words.note: Doubled: “he replies” is يَرُدُّ. With -tu the doubled letter splits in two, as in the example.

words.example_meaning_en: We passed by the market on the way.
words.note: “He passes” is يَمُرُّ. The same root as مَرَّة, “a time, once”.

words.example_meaning_en: Yūsuf took the key and went out.
words.note: Hamzated: “he takes” is يَأْخُذُ, but “take!” is خُذْ, with no hamza.

words.example_meaning_en: I asked the teacher a question.
words.note: The hamza is the middle root letter; its seat changes with the vowels, as in سُؤَال.
“He begins” is يَبْدَأُ. The same root as فِي الْبِدَايَةِ, “at the beginning”.

words.example_meaning_en: The verb after لَمْ is jussive.
words.note: Only verbs can be jussive, just as only nouns can be مَجْرُور.
A grammar word. The past form is الْمَاضِي.

words.example_meaning_en: I’ll wait until the train arrives.
words.note: Before a present verb, as here, the verb ends in fatḥa. Also “even”.
يَكُونُ loses its long ū after لَمْ, not just its last vowel.
From يَفْهَمُونَ: after لَمْ the ending is -ū, written with an alif that isn’t said.
لَا with the jussive is “don’t”, so تَنْسَى loses its final ā. To a woman: لَا تَنْسَيْ.

words.example_meaning_en: الدَّرْسُ is the passive subject in “The lesson was explained”.
words.note: Literally “deputy of the doer”: it takes the doer’s place, and is nominative like it.

words.example_meaning_en: The writer of this story is unknown.
words.note: Grammar calls a passive verb الْمَبْنِيُّ لِلْمَجْهُولِ, “built for the unknown”.
Passive vowels: ḍamma, then kasra. “She gave birth” is the active وَلَدَتْ.

words.example_meaning_en: It was said that the museum is closed today.
words.note: The passive of قَالَ: no speaker is named. “It is said” is يُقَالُ.

words.example_meaning_en: The news item was published this morning.
words.note: News often uses the passive when the doer isn’t the point. “He published” is نَشَرَ.

words.example_meaning_en: My bag was stolen on the train.
words.note: With the passive, the thief needn’t be named. “He stole” is سَرَقَ.
Plural تَقَارِير.

words.meaning_en: who, which, that (for a masculine noun)
words.example_meaning_en: Where is the pen that was here?
words.note: Written with one ل, though the l is said doubled.

words.meaning_en: who, which, that (for a feminine noun)
words.example_meaning_en: The city that I visited is beautiful.
words.note: Also for plural things, as in الْكُتُبُ الَّتِي, “the books that”.

words.meaning_en: who (for men, or a mixed group)
words.example_meaning_en: The students who passed are happy.
words.note: Only for people. Its form stays the same in every case.

words.example_meaning_en: What is the pronoun in this sentence?
words.note: Plural ضَمَائِر. Also “conscience”.

words.example_meaning_en: He is a person who loves reading.
words.note: Plural أَشْخَاص.

words.example_meaning_en: My neighbour who lives above us is a doctor.
words.note: Plural جِيرَان. A woman neighbour is جَارَة.
Often left untranslated: it stresses the statement.

words.example_meaning_en: I know that the lesson is difficult.
words.note: Not أَنْ, which comes before a verb.

words.example_meaning_en: Perhaps the library is open now.
words.note: Works like إِنَّ, so its noun ends in -a here.
Works like كَانَ. The same root as صَبَاح, “morning”.

words.example_meaning_en: My sister is still at university.
words.note: Literally “hasn’t stopped”. In the present: لَا يَزَالُ.

words.meaning_en: predicate (in grammar); a piece of news
words.note: In grammar, what is said about the subject. Plural أَخْبَار, “news”.
The same root as اِجْتِهَاد, “hard work”.

words.example_ar: ذَكَرَتِ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ أَنَّ الِامْتِحَانَ يَوْمَ الْأَحَدِ.
words.example_meaning_en: The teacher mentioned that the exam is on Sunday.
words.note: Followed by أَنَّ, while قَالَ is followed by إِنَّ.

words.example_meaning_en: The manager explained the reason for the delay.
words.note: The same root as وَاضِح, “clear”.

words.example_meaning_en: Laylā confirmed that she will come.
words.note: Stronger than قَالَ: the speaker presents it as certain.

words.example_meaning_en: I think the idea is good.
words.note: For a belief, not a fact. Form VIII: “he believes” is يَعْتَقِدُ.
A supposition, which may be wrong. “He thinks” is يَظُنُّ.

words.example_meaning_en: He claimed he hadn’t seen the message.
words.note: Often used when the writer doubts the claim.

words.example_meaning_en: If Salmā comes, we’ll go together.
words.note: Usually followed by a past verb, even about the future.
Both verbs are jussive here. Not إِنَّ, “indeed”.

words.example_meaning_en: If I had time, I would visit you.
words.note: The result often starts with لَـ, as here.

words.example_meaning_en: If it weren’t for your help, I’d have been late.
words.note: A noun follows it, in the nominative.
Literally “except if”.
Plural شُرُوط.
In an either-or question, “or” is أَمْ.

words.example_ar: أَسْتَيْقِظُ مُبَكِّرًا لِكَيْ أَصِلَ فِي الْمَوْعِدِ.
words.example_meaning_en: I get up early so that I arrive on time.
words.note: The verb after it ends in fatḥa: أَصِلَ.
Before a noun; before a verb, لِكَيْ is usual.

words.example_meaning_en: I was late because of the traffic.
words.note: Before a noun. Before a sentence, use لِأَنَّ.

words.example_meaning_en: I went out although the weather was cold.
words.note: As after أَنَّ alone, the noun after it ends in -a: الْجَوَّ.
Before a noun. Also بِالرَّغْمِ مِنْ.

words.example_ar: أَنَا أُحِبُّ الشَّايَ، أَمَّا أَخِي فَيُحِبُّ الْقَهْوَةَ.
words.example_meaning_en: I like tea; as for my brother, he likes coffee.
words.note: What follows the topic starts with فَـ, as in the example.

words.example_meaning_en: My father is reading, while my mother is writing.
words.note: It can mean “while” in time, or set two things side by side, as here.

words.example_meaning_en: The text is short and easy.
words.note: Plural نُصُوص.

words.example_meaning_en: This text has no vowel marks.
words.note: The same root as مُشْكِلَة, “problem”.

words.example_meaning_en: What is the vowel mark on this letter?
words.note: Plural حَرَكَات. In everyday use, “movement”.

words.example_meaning_en: There’s a fatḥa on the bāʾ.
words.note: From فَتَحَ, “he opened”: the mouth opens for a.

words.example_meaning_en: There’s a ḍamma at the end of the subject.
words.note: From ضَمَّ, “he brought together”, as the lips do for u.

words.example_meaning_en: There’s a kasra under the bāʾ.
words.note: From كَسَرَ, “he broke”.

words.example_meaning_en: In لَمْ there’s a sukūn on the mīm.
words.note: Also “stillness”: the letter rests, with no vowel.

words.example_meaning_en: In مُعَلِّم there’s a shadda on the lām.
words.note: The letter it sits on is held twice as long.

words.example_ar: هَلْ هَذِهِ الْكَلِمَةُ فِعْلٌ أَمِ اسْمٌ؟
words.example_meaning_en: Is this word a verb or a noun?
words.note: Plural أَفْعَال. In grammar, اِسْم is “noun”.
Unvowelled ذهب can also be ذَهَبَ, “he went”: the sentence decides.
Unvowelled شعر can also be “poetry”, as in الشِّعْرُ الْعَرَبِيُّ, “Arabic poetry”, or the verb in شَعَرَ بِالْبَرْدِ, “he felt cold”.
Unvowelled ملك can also be مَلَكَ, “he owned”, or مُلْك, “property”.

words.example_meaning_en: My grandfather lives in a village.
words.note: Unvowelled جد can also be جِدّ, “seriousness”, as in جِدًّا, “very”.
Without the shadda, حَمَام is “pigeons”: one mark can change the word.

words.example_meaning_en: There are two possibilities for this word.
words.note: Plural اِحْتِمَالَات. Keep both open until the sentence decides.
Plural مَوْضُوعَات. The same root as وَضَعَ, “he put”.
The same root as رَأْس, “head”.

words.example_meaning_en: He studies Arabic in addition to his job.
words.note: Adds a further point to the one before.

words.example_ar: الشَّقَّةُ صَغِيرَةٌ، وَمِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ أُخْرَى سِعْرُهَا مُنَاسِبٌ.
words.example_meaning_en: The flat is small; on the other hand, its price is reasonable.
words.note: Often after مِنْ نَاحِيَةٍ, “on one hand”.

words.example_meaning_en: Salmā is a doctor, and so is her sister.
words.note: كَـ, “like”, with ذَلِكَ, “that”.
After أَوَّلًا, “first”. Then ثَالِثًا, “thirdly”.

words.example_meaning_en: In short, the trip was a success.
words.note: Closes a paragraph by summing up.

words.example_meaning_en: I’m reading a short novel this month.
words.note: Also “account, version (of events)”.
Plural مَجَلَّات.
Plural صَفَحَات, as here.

words.example_meaning_en: I understood the general meaning of the story.
words.note: The opposite is خَاصّ, “particular”.
The opposite is مُمِلّ, “boring”.
Also بِلَا, as in بِلَا مُشْكِلَةٍ, “no problem”.
Form IV: “he finishes” is يُنْهِي. The same root as فِي النِّهَايَةِ, “in the end”.

words.example_meaning_en: The student posed an important question.
words.note: More formal than سَأَلَ, “he asked”.

words.example_meaning_en: The professor gave a lecture on history.
words.note: Literally “threw a lecture”: learn the pair, not each word.

words.example_meaning_en: The minister made a visit to the school.
words.note: Formal, common in news: قَامَ بِـ with a noun is “carried out”. On its own, قَامَ is “he stood up”.

words.example_meaning_en: She got a certificate in Arabic.
words.note: On its own, حَصَلَ can mean “it happened”.

words.example_meaning_en: I took part in a reading competition.
words.note: “Taking part” is مُشَارَكَة.

words.example_meaning_en: I took a photo of the sea.
words.note: Formal Arabic prefers this to أَخَذَ, the everyday “take”.

words.example_meaning_en: We had a lovely time with the family.
words.note: In the present: يَقْضِي وَقْتًا, “he spends time”. Spending money is أَنْفَقَ.

words.example_meaning_en: I listened to the recording twice.
words.note: Form VIII of the root of أَسْمَعُ, “I hear”: listening on purpose. It takes إِلَى.
Singular تَفْصِيل.

words.example_meaning_en: I paused the recording after the first sentence.
words.note: Form IV of وَقَفَ, “he stopped”: to stop something.

words.meaning_en: section (of a recording or text); syllable
words.example_meaning_en: I listened to the difficult section again.
words.note: Plural مَقَاطِع.
The verbal noun of فَهِمَ, “he understood”.

words.example_meaning_en: I understood the news item on my own.
words.note: Without help. “On your own” is بِمُفْرَدِكَ.
بِسُرْعَةٍ is “quickly”; its opposite is بِبُطْءٍ, “slowly”.

words.example_ar: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَفْهَمَ الْكَلَامَ بِسُرْعَتِهِ الطَّبِيعِيَّةِ.
words.example_meaning_en: I want to understand speech at its natural speed.
words.note: The same root as طَبْعًا, “of course”.
The same root as كَلِمَة, “word”, and يَتَكَلَّمُ, “he speaks”.

words.example_meaning_en: There are two speakers in the recording.
words.note: The same root as مُحَادَثَة, “conversation”. A woman speaker is مُتَحَدِّثَة.

words.example_meaning_en: I repeated the sentence after the speaker.
words.note: Form II. “Repetition” is تَكْرَار.

words.example_meaning_en: Her tone of voice is calm.
words.note: In phonetics, نَبْر is the stress on a syllable.

words.example_ar: لَا تُنْطَقُ هَمْزَةُ الْوَصْلِ فِي وَسَطِ الْكَلَامِ.
words.example_meaning_en: The joining hamza isn’t said in the middle of speech.
words.note: The first vowel of the article and of words like اِسْم, dropped after another word.
Plural أَمْثِلَة. “For example” is مَثَلًا.

words.example_meaning_en: How long have you worked here?
words.note: On its own, مُنْذُ is “since” or “ago”: مُنْذُ سَنَةٍ, “a year ago”.

words.meaning_en: what do you mean? (to a man)
words.example_meaning_en: What do you mean by this word?
words.note: To a woman: مَاذَا تَقْصِدِينَ؟
The same root as مَعْنَى, “meaning”. In speech it’s also a filler, “I mean”.
Shows you’re listening, and invites more.
The noun after it is genitive and has no article.

words.example_ar: قُلْتَ إِنَّ الدَّرْسَ سَهْلٌ. كَيْفَ ذَلِكَ؟
words.example_meaning_en: You said the lesson is easy. How so?
words.note: Asks how or why something just said is so.

words.example_meaning_en: In my opinion, the film is very long.
words.note: رَأْي is “opinion”. To ask for one: مَا رَأْيُكَ؟

words.example_meaning_en: I don’t mean today, I mean tomorrow.
words.note: Puts right what you said, or what someone understood.

words.example_meaning_en: I understand your view, but I don’t agree.
words.note: Softer: أُوَافِقُ جُزْئِيًّا, “I partly agree”.

words.example_ar: بِعِبَارَةٍ أُخْرَى، نَحْتَاجُ إِلَى وَقْتٍ أَكْثَرَ.
words.example_meaning_en: In other words, we need more time.
words.note: Introduces a paraphrase. عِبَارَة is “expression, phrase”.

words.example_meaning_en: The trip takes about two hours.
words.note: The same root as قَرِيب, “near”.

words.example_meaning_en: That’s true, but time is short.
words.note: The same root as the word for “health”, as in صِحَّتُهُ جَيِّدَةٌ, “his health is good”.

words.example_ar: أَقْرَأُ صَفْحَةً وَاحِدَةً عَلَى الْأَقَلِّ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
words.example_meaning_en: I read at least one page a day.
words.note: The same root as قَلِيلًا, “a little”.

words.example_meaning_en: The newsreader speaks in Standard Arabic.
words.note: Short for الْعَرَبِيَّةُ الْفُصْحَى, “the most eloquent Arabic”.

words.example_meaning_en: My grandfather speaks in his village’s dialect.
words.note: Plural لَهَجَات.
Plural لُكْنَات. You’ll also hear it said with an a-vowel, لَكْنَة.

words.example_meaning_en: We speak colloquial Arabic at home.
words.note: The everyday spoken language, as against الْفُصْحَى.
The opposite is غَيْرُ رَسْمِيٍّ, “informal”.
A woman newsreader is مُذِيعَة.

words.example_meaning_en: I noticed a difference in pronunciation.
words.note: Plural اِخْتِلَافَات. “Different” is مُخْتَلِف.

words.example_ar: عَلَى سَبِيلِ الْمِثَالِ، أَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى الْأَخْبَارِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
words.example_meaning_en: For example, I listen to the news every morning.
words.note: More formal than مَثَلًا.
The same root as قَدَّمَ, “he presented”.

words.example_meaning_en: The last sentence is the paragraph’s conclusion.
words.note: From خَتَمَ, “he concluded, he sealed”.

words.example_meaning_en: This is how I revise the lesson every evening.
words.note: Often closes a paragraph by linking back to its point.

words.example_meaning_en: The sentences in this paragraph hang together.
words.note: The same root as رَبَطَ, “he tied, he linked”.

words.example_ar: أَدْرُسُ يَوْمِيًّا، أَيْ سَبْعَةَ أَيَّامٍ فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ.
words.example_meaning_en: I study daily, that is, seven days a week.
words.note: Explains or restates what came before. Not أَيّ, “which”.
After the name or title in a formal letter. For a woman: مُحْتَرَمَة.

words.example_meaning_en: Please reply as soon as possible.
words.note: Formal “please”, followed by what you ask for, as a noun or with أَنْ.
On its own, بَرِيد is “post, mail”.

words.example_meaning_en: You will find the picture attached.
words.note: Plural مُرْفَقَات, “attachments”.

words.example_meaning_en: I have an enquiry about the course.
words.note: Asking for an explanation. The same root as تَفْسِير, “explanation”.

words.example_meaning_en: I begin the letter with a short greeting.
words.note: A usual opening is تَحِيَّةً طَيِّبَةً وَبَعْدُ, and a usual closing is مَعَ التَّحِيَّةِ, “with regards”.

words.example_meaning_en: Thank you in advance for your help.
words.note: A polite close to a request.

words.example_meaning_en: I read an article about education.
words.note: Also مَقَال. The same root as قَالَ, “he said”.

words.example_meaning_en: I summarised the article in three sentences.
words.note: Form II. “A summary” is مُلَخَّص.

words.example_meaning_en: The writer pointed to the traffic problem.
words.note: A reporting verb: it keeps the point the writer’s.

words.example_meaning_en: I wrote down only the important points.
words.note: Plural نِقَاط. In punctuation, the full stop.

words.example_ar: لَا تُضِفْ شَيْئًا لَيْسَ فِي النَّصِّ.
words.example_meaning_en: Don’t add anything that isn’t in the text.
words.note: Form IV, hollow: “he adds” is يُضِيفُ. After لَا, “don’t”, it shortens to تُضِفْ.

words.example_meaning_en: In general, the text is clear.
words.note: Sums up the whole, without the details.

words.example_meaning_en: In سُؤَال the hamza sits on a wāw.
words.note: Its seat depends on the vowels around it.

words.example_meaning_en: غُرْفَة ends in a tāʾ marbūṭa.
words.note: Literally “tied tāʾ”: said -a at a pause, and -at when its ending is said, as in غُرْفَةُ النَّوْمِ.

words.example_meaning_en: عَلَى is written with an alif maqṣūra.
words.note: It looks like ي without dots, and is said ā.

words.example_ar: ضَعْ عَلَامَةَ الِاسْتِفْهَامِ فِي آخِرِ السُّؤَالِ.
words.example_meaning_en: Put a question mark at the end of the question.
words.note: In Arabic it faces the other way: ؟
In Arabic it’s written ، turned the other way.

words.example_meaning_en: There’s one mistake in this sentence.
words.note: The hamza sits on alif after a fatḥa. In the plural, as in أَخْطَاءٌ كَثِيرَةٌ, “many mistakes”, it stands on the line after a long ā.

words.example_ar: رَاجَعْتُ الْإِمْلَاءَ قَبْلَ أَنْ أُرْسِلَ الرِّسَالَةَ.
words.example_meaning_en: I checked the spelling before I sent the message.
words.note: The verbal noun of أَمْلَى, “he dictated”.
Form II of the root of صَحِيح, “correct”.
The same root as أَسْوَد, “black”.
Plural تَعْلِيقَات, as here.

words.meaning_en: he did again; he gave back
words.note: With a verbal noun it means “do again”: أَعَادَ الْقِرَاءَةَ, “he read it again”.

words.example_meaning_en: My writing has improved a lot.
words.note: Form V. The same root as أَحْسَن, “better”.
Feminine is مُؤَنَّث.
Form III, often with بَيْنَ. “Comparison” is مُقَارَنَة.

words.example_meaning_en: The two sources share a topic.
words.note: The same root as شَارَكَ فِي, “took part in”.

words.example_meaning_en: The two sources agree on the general idea.
words.note: Form VIII, from the root of مُوَافِق, “agreed”. It takes عَلَى.

words.example_meaning_en: The second source differs from the first.
words.note: “Differs from” is اِخْتَلَفَ عَنْ.

words.example_meaning_en: The cause of the problem is unclear.
words.note: Makes an opposite with the word after it, as in غَيْرُ مُمْكِنٍ, “impossible”.
From وَثِقَ, “he trusted”; in full, مَوْثُوق بِهِ.

words.example_meaning_en: The teacher explained the lesson to us with examples.
words.note: “An explanation” is شَرْح.
Past كَفَى. “It isn’t enough” is لَا يَكْفِي.
With other endings: وَحْدِي, “on my own”, and وَحْدَهَا, “by herself”.

words.example_meaning_en: I’ll explain the idea in simple words.
words.note: The opposite is مُعَقَّد, “complicated”.

words.example_meaning_en: In conclusion, thank you for listening.
words.note: Closes a talk or a piece of writing.

words.example_ar: إِذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ هَذَا وَاضِحًا فَاسْأَلُونِي.
words.example_meaning_en: If that isn’t clear, ask me.
words.note: Checks that your listeners have followed.

words.example_meaning_en: One of the listeners asked me a question.
words.note: From اِسْتَمَعَ, “he listened”.
For a woman: مُتَأَكِّدَة. The same root as أَكَّدَ, “he confirmed”.

words.example_meaning_en: A hard question; let me think a little.
words.note: دَعْنِي is “let me”. The same root as فِكْرَة, “idea”.

words.example_ar: فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ، لَمْ أَقْرَأْ هَذَا الْكِتَابَ.
words.example_meaning_en: Actually, I haven’t read this book.
words.note: حَقِيقَة is “truth, fact”.

words.example_ar: عَلَى حَدِّ عِلْمِي، الْمَكْتَبَةُ مَفْتُوحَةٌ يَوْمَ السَّبْتِ.
words.example_meaning_en: As far as I know, the library is open on Saturday.
words.note: Marks the limit of what you know.

words.example_meaning_en: Honestly, I hadn’t thought about that.
words.note: صَرِيح is “frank”.

words.example_meaning_en: I chose this course because it’s in the evening.
words.note: Form VIII, hollow: “he chooses” is يَخْتَارُ.
Also “relies on”.
The verbal noun of تَعَلَّمَ, “he learned”.
“Patient” is صَبُور.

words.example_meaning_en: I’m looking for a book that suits my level.
words.note: The same root as يُنَاسِبُكَ, “it suits you”.

words.example_ar: أَكْتُبُ فِي سِجِلٍّ مَا أَقْرَأُ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ.
words.example_meaning_en: I write what I read each day in a log.
words.note: The same root as تَسْجِيل, “recording”.
Plural أَوْلَوِيَّات.

words.example_meaning_en: I do one exercise every morning.
words.note: Plural تَمَارِين.
From دَرَجَة, “step, degree”.
Plural مَهَارَات. The four: الْقِرَاءَة, الْكِتَابَة, الِاسْتِمَاع and الْمُحَادَثَة.
A weak point is نُقْطَةُ ضَعْفٍ.

words.example_meaning_en: This recording is evidence of my progress.
words.note: Plural أَدِلَّة. Also a guidebook.
“Independence” is اِسْتِقْلَال.
The same root as خَاصّ, “particular”.
Plural مَرَاحِل. The same root as رِحْلَة, “trip”.

words.example_ar: أَنَا قَادِرٌ عَلَى فَهْمِ الْأَخْبَارِ الْبَسِيطَةِ.
words.example_meaning_en: I’m able to understand simple news.
words.note: Like أَسْتَطِيعُ, but with عَلَى and a noun.

words.example_meaning_en: The minister attended the opening of the exhibition.
words.note: From اِفْتَتَحَ, “to open (formally)”. A headline often starts with it.

words.example_meaning_en: The channel interrupted the programme for breaking news.
words.note: Plural أَخْبَارٌ عَاجِلَةٌ.

words.example_meaning_en: The report didn't name the party responsible.
words.note: Plural جِهَات. Also “side, direction”.

words.example_meaning_en: I read the story in today's newspaper.
words.note: Plural صُحُف. A journalist is صَحَفِيّ.

words.example_meaning_en: The correspondent reported the news from the airport.
words.note: For a woman: مُرَاسِلَة. Plural مُرَاسِلُونَ.

words.example_meaning_en: The number of participants reached fifty people.
words.note: For a woman: مُشَارِكَة. From شَارَكَ, “to take part”.

words.example_meaning_en: An accident happened on the motorway.
words.note: Plural حَوَادِث.

words.example_meaning_en: The university announced the date of the exams.
words.note: Present يُعْلِنُ. The noun إِعْلَان means “announcement” or “advert”.

words.example_meaning_en: The spokesperson stated that the road is closed.
words.note: Present يُفِيدُ, which also means “to be useful”, as in مُفِيد.

words.example_ar: بِحَسَبِ الْمَوْقِعِ، يَصِلُ الْقِطَارُ فِي الثَّامِنَةِ.
words.example_meaning_en: According to the website, the train arrives at eight.
words.note: Also حَسَبَ, with the same meaning.
Present يَنْفِي. The opposite of أَكَّدَ, “he confirmed”.

words.example_ar: قَالَ مَسْؤُولٌ فِي الْوِزَارَةِ إِنَّ الْعَمَلَ سَيَبْدَأُ قَرِيبًا.
words.example_meaning_en: An official in the ministry said that the work will start soon.
words.note: Plural مَسْؤُولُونَ. مَسْؤُولٌ عَنْ means “responsible for”.

words.example_ar: رَجَّحَ الْخُبَرَاءُ أَنْ يَرْتَفِعَ عَدَدُ الزُّوَّارِ.
words.example_meaning_en: Experts considered it likely that the number of visitors would rise.
words.note: A likelihood, not a fact. The passive يُرَجَّحُ means “it is thought likely”.

words.example_ar: ذَكَرَتْ مَصَادِرُ مُطَّلِعَةٌ أَنَّ الِاجْتِمَاعَ تَأَجَّلَ.
words.example_meaning_en: Informed sources said that the meeting had been postponed.
words.note: Sources without a name: the claim is still unconfirmed.
Present يَرْتَفِعُ. The noun اِرْتِفَاع means “rise” or “height”.
Present يَنْخَفِضُ. The noun اِنْخِفَاض means “fall, decrease”.

words.example_meaning_en: The pass rate is high this year.
words.note: Plural نِسَب. نِسْبَةٌ مِئَوِيَّةٌ means “a percentage”.

words.example_ar: نَجَحَ ثَمَانُونَ فِي الْمِئَةِ مِنَ الطُّلَّابِ.
words.example_meaning_en: Eighty per cent of the students passed.
words.note: Also بِالْمِئَةِ, with the same meaning.

words.example_ar: يَزُورُ الْمَتْحَفَ مِلْيُونُ زَائِرٍ كُلَّ سَنَةٍ.
words.example_meaning_en: A million visitors visit the museum every year.
words.note: Plural مَلَايِين. Two million: مِلْيُونَانِ.

words.example_meaning_en: The price became double what it was.
words.note: Plural أَضْعَاف, as in ثَلَاثَةُ أَضْعَافٍ, “three times as much”.

words.example_meaning_en: The students' average age is twenty.
words.note: Also an adjective, “medium”: حَجْمٌ مُتَوَسِّطٌ.

words.example_meaning_en: The channel did an interview with the writer.
words.note: Plural مُقَابَلَات. أَجْرَى مُقَابَلَةً means “to conduct an interview”.

words.example_meaning_en: The presenter asked the guest for his opinion.
words.note: Plural ضُيُوف. For a woman: ضَيْفَة.
Used with مِنْ. The noun: تَهَرُّب.

words.example_meaning_en: Check the quotation before you publish it.
words.note: Plural اِقْتِبَاسَات. Check it against the recording.

words.example_meaning_en: I reworded the idea in my own words.
words.note: أَعَادَ صِيَاغَةَ means “to rephrase”: a paraphrase, not a quotation.

words.meaning_en: interviewer; the other party in a dialogue
words.example_meaning_en: The interviewer asked a difficult question.
words.note: For a woman: مُحَاوِرَة. From حِوَار, “dialogue”.

words.example_meaning_en: The guest didn't make his position clear.
words.note: Plural مَوَاقِف. Also “a bus stop” or “a car park”.

words.example_ar: أَسْتَمِعُ إِلَى نَشْرَةِ الْأَخْبَارِ كُلَّ صَبَاحٍ.
words.example_meaning_en: I listen to the news bulletin every morning.
words.note: نَشْرَة alone is a bulletin, leaflet or newsletter.

words.example_meaning_en: An update to the story was published an hour later.
words.note: Plural تَحْدِيثَات. From حَدَّثَ, “to update”.

words.example_meaning_en: Contradictory reports reached us about the incident.
words.note: تَنَاقُض means “a contradiction”.
The opposite: مُؤَكَّد, “confirmed”.

words.meaning_en: as he put it, by his account
words.example_meaning_en: The project is a success, as he put it.
words.note: Keeps a claim with its speaker. For a woman: عَلَى حَدِّ قَوْلِهَا.

words.example_ar: الْبَيْتُ صَغِيرٌ بِالْمُقَارَنَةِ مَعَ بَيْتِنَا الْقَدِيمِ.
words.example_meaning_en: The house is small compared with our old house.
words.note: مُقَارَنَة alone means “a comparison”.

words.example_meaning_en: Here is the news in brief.
words.note: Also an adjective, “brief”: تَقْرِيرٌ مُوجَزٌ.

words.example_meaning_en: The writer has a strong argument.
words.note: Plural حُجَج. Often with دَلِيل, “evidence”.

words.example_meaning_en: This is a claim without evidence.
words.note: Plural اِدِّعَاءَات. From اِدَّعَى, “to claim”.

words.example_meaning_en: Beware of generalising in the article.
words.note: From عَمَّمَ, “to generalise”.
From أَقْنَعَ, “to convince”.
Present يَدْعَمُ. The noun دَعْم means “support”.

words.example_ar: هَذَا الْمِثَالُ لَيْسَ ذَا صِلَةٍ بِالْمَوْضُوعِ.
words.example_meaning_en: This example isn't relevant to the topic.
words.note: For a feminine noun: ذَاتُ صِلَةٍ.
With the article: الْكَافِي. From كَفَى, “to be enough”.
Weaker: مِنَ الْمُمْكِنِ أَنْ, “it is possible that”.

words.example_meaning_en: It seems that the library is closed today.
words.note: With an adjective: يَبْدُو سَعِيدًا, “he looks happy”.

words.example_meaning_en: I'll certainly come to the party.
words.note: The same root as أَكَّدَ, “he confirmed”.

words.example_meaning_en: I usually study in the morning.
words.note: غَالِبًا مَا with a habit means “usually, mostly”. Before a prediction it means “most likely”, close to عَلَى الْأَرْجَحِ.

words.example_meaning_en: The plan is successful to some extent.
words.note: Limits a claim without taking it back.

words.example_meaning_en: I don't rule out the train being late.
words.note: From اِسْتَبْعَدَ, “to rule out, think unlikely”.

words.example_meaning_en: He will most probably arrive in the evening.
words.note: The same root as رَجَّحَ, “to think likely”.

words.example_meaning_en: There is implicit criticism in what he says.
words.note: ضِمْنِيًّا means “implicitly”. The opposite: صَرِيح.
Also “frank”: كُنْ صَرِيحًا مَعِي.
Plural نِيَّات.

words.example_meaning_en: There is another interpretation of this sentence.
words.note: Plural تَفْسِيرَات. From فَسَّرَ, “to explain, interpret”.
Used with بِ: يُوحِي بِأَنَّ, “suggests that”.
From اِفْتَرَضَ, “to assume”.
ظَاهِرُ النَّصِّ, “the surface meaning of the text”.

words.example_ar: كَانَ مُتْعَبًا، وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ أَكْمَلَ الْعَمَلَ.
words.example_meaning_en: He was tired; nevertheless, he finished the work.
words.note: Often with وَ before it: وَمَعَ ذَلِكَ.

words.example_meaning_en: I have one objection to the plan.
words.note: From اِعْتَرَضَ عَلَى, “to object to”.

words.example_meaning_en: The writer refuted the opposing view with evidence.
words.note: Present يُفَنِّدُ. The noun تَفْنِيد means “rebuttal”.

words.example_ar: صَحِيحٌ أَنَّ الطَّرِيقَ طَوِيلٌ، لَكِنَّهُ آمِنٌ.
words.example_meaning_en: It's true that the road is long, but it's safe.
words.note: Builds on صَحِيح, “true”. Usually followed by لَكِنَّ, “but”.

words.example_meaning_en: There is exaggeration in what was said.
words.note: From بَالَغَ, “to exaggerate”.

words.example_meaning_en: Your question is a fair one.
words.note: Said of a reason or a question: سَبَبٌ وَجِيهٌ.
أَرْضِيَّة alone means “a floor” or “a basis”.

words.example_meaning_en: A calm discussion took place among the students.
words.note: From نَاقَشَ, “to discuss”.
From وَضَّحَ, “to clarify”.
Also “role”: دَوْرٌ مُهِمٌّ.

words.example_ar: الْخُلَاصَةُ أَنَّنَا نَحْتَاجُ إِلَى وَقْتٍ أَطْوَلَ.
words.example_meaning_en: The upshot is that we need more time.
words.note: خُلَاصَةُ الْقَوْلِ means “in short”.
From تَفَهَّمَ, “to show understanding for”.
From قَاطَعَ, “to interrupt”.

words.example_ar: بِنَاءً عَلَى هَذِهِ الْأَرْقَامِ، أَقْتَرِحُ خُطَّةً جَدِيدَةً.
words.example_meaning_en: Based on these figures, I suggest a new plan.
words.note: Points to the evidence behind a view.
From طَابَقَ, “to match, agree with”.

words.example_meaning_en: A verbal sentence begins with a verb.
words.note: One that begins with a noun: جُمْلَةٌ اسْمِيَّةٌ.

words.example_meaning_en: The order of the words changes the emphasis.
words.note: From رَتَّبَ, “to arrange”.
The opposite: مُذَكَّر.
A thing or an animal is غَيْرُ عَاقِلٍ.

words.example_meaning_en: Putting the subject first sometimes adds emphasis.
words.note: Also “presentation”: تَقْدِيمُ عَرْضٍ.

words.example_ar: فِي جُمْلَةِ الْمُعَلِّمَةُ وَصَلَتْ، الْمُعَلِّمَةُ مُبْتَدَأٌ.
words.example_meaning_en: In al-muʿallimatu waṣalat, al-muʿallima is the mubtadaʾ.
words.note: Its partner is خَبَر, the predicate. A subject placed before its verb is a مُبْتَدَأ, not a فَاعِل.

words.example_meaning_en: There is a ḥāl in the sentence jāʾa rākiḍan.
words.note: The grammar term. The everyday word is the one in كَيْفَ حَالُكَ؟

words.example_meaning_en: The tamyīz clarifies a number or a quantity.
words.note: From مَيَّزَ, “to distinguish”.
From اِبْتَسَمَ, “to smile”.

words.example_meaning_en: He went out in a hurry.
words.note: From أَسْرَعَ, “to hurry”.

words.example_meaning_en: We bought a large quantity of rice.
words.note: From كَمْ, “how much, how many”.
From غَضِبَ, “to be angry”. Here غَاضِبًا is a ḥāl.
What grows comes after it in the accusative.

words.example_meaning_en: There are a hundred chairs in the hall.
words.note: Two hundred: مِئَتَانِ.

words.example_meaning_en: There are eleven players in the team.
words.note: With a feminine noun: إِحْدَى عَشْرَةَ.

words.example_meaning_en: A thousand people attended the conference.
words.note: Plural آلَاف. Two thousand: أَلْفَانِ.
Other examples: مَسَاجِد, and many names like زَيْنَب.

words.example_meaning_en: There is tanwīn at the end of the word kitābun.
words.note: The endings -un, -an and -in: كِتَابٌ, كِتَابًا and كِتَابٍ.

words.example_ar: تَأَكَّدْتُ مِنَ الْقَاعِدَةِ فِي مَرْجِعٍ مَوْثُوقٍ.
words.example_meaning_en: I checked the rule in a reliable reference.
words.note: Plural مَرَاجِع.

words.example_meaning_en: In thalāthatu kutubin, the counted noun is kutub.
words.note: From عَدَّ, “to count”.
Also إِلَّا أَنَّ, “except that, however”.

words.example_ar: لَمْ يَتَأَخَّرْ كَسَلًا، وَإِنَّمَا بِسَبَبِ الْمَطَرِ.
words.example_meaning_en: He wasn't late out of laziness, but because of the rain.
words.note: After a negative it often comes as وَإِنَّمَا, “but rather”. At the start of a sentence it restricts: “it is only…”.
It comes after what it limits.

words.example_meaning_en: No doubt the exercise is useful.
words.note: Also لَا شَكَّ فِي ذَلِكَ, “there is no doubt about that”.
بِاسْتِثْنَاءِ means “with the exception of”.

words.example_meaning_en: The negative particle changes the meaning of the sentence.
words.note: The same root as نَفَى, “he denied”.
Also لَمْ يَأْتِ أَحَدٌ, “nobody came”.

words.example_ar: يَحْتَاجُ النَّصُّ إِلَى تَدْقِيقٍ قَبْلَ النَّشْرِ.
words.example_meaning_en: The text needs checking before publication.
words.note: From دَقَّقَ, “to check carefully”. دَقِيق means “precise”.

words.example_meaning_en: Is there an alternative to this word?
words.note: Plural بَدَائِل.

words.example_meaning_en: There is an ambiguity in the sentence.
words.note: غَامِض means “unclear, ambiguous”.

words.example_meaning_en: I dropped the hamza by mistake.
words.note: The noun سَهْو means “an oversight, a slip”.

words.example_meaning_en: Leaving out the negative particle reverses the meaning.
words.note: From حَذَفَ, “to delete, leave out”.
Plural صِيَغ. The same root as صِيَاغَة, “wording”.

words.example_meaning_en: The translator conveyed the meaning faithfully.
words.note: أَمَانَة means “honesty, faithfulness”.

words.example_meaning_en: I sketched an outline for the essay before writing.
words.note: Plural مُخَطَّطَات. From خَطَّطَ, “to plan”.
Plural عَنَاصِر.

words.example_meaning_en: The writer defended his thesis with evidence.
words.note: Also “a doctoral thesis”. Plural أُطْرُوحَات.

words.example_meaning_en: The essay turns on three themes.
words.note: Plural مَحَاوِر.

words.example_meaning_en: The flow of ideas is clear.
words.note: From سِلْسِلَة, “chain, series”.
From اِسْتَنْتَجَ, “to conclude, infer”. The same root as نَتِيجَة, “result”.
مُضَادّ means “opposing, anti-”.
Plural عُرُوض. Also “an offer”: عَرْضٌ خَاصٌّ.

words.example_meaning_en: She spoke in front of a large audience.
words.note: Plural جَمَاهِير.

words.example_meaning_en: The lecturer addressed the topic of energy.
words.note: Present يَتَنَاوَلُ. Also “to have (a meal)”: تَنَاوَلْنَا الْغَدَاءَ.

words.example_ar: لَا تَقْرَأْ كُلَّ شَرِيحَةٍ بِصَوْتٍ عَالٍ.
words.note: Plural شَرَائِح. Also “a slice”.
لِمُدَّةِ means “for (a period)”: لِمُدَّةِ سَاعَةٍ.
بِنَفْسِ الْوَتِيرَةِ means “at the same pace”.

words.example_meaning_en: I'll now move on to the second point.
words.note: A signpost in a talk. Also “to move (house)”.

words.meaning_en: I take it from what you say that
words.example_ar: أَفْهَمُ مِنْ كَلَامِكَ أَنَّكَ تُفَضِّلُ الْقِرَاءَةَ الْوَرَقِيَّةَ.
words.example_meaning_en: I take it from what you say that you prefer reading on paper.
words.note: A way to check you have understood before answering.

words.example_ar: لَا أَعْرِفُ بِالضَّبْطِ مَتَى يَبْدَأُ الْعَرْضُ.
words.example_meaning_en: I don't know exactly when the presentation starts.
words.note: On its own as a reply: “Exactly!”
From اِفْتِرَاض, “assumption”. Also “virtual”: صَفٌّ افْتِرَاضِيٌّ.

words.example_meaning_en: This question is outside the scope of the research.
words.note: Plural نِطَاقَات.

words.example_meaning_en: I don't want to answer by guessing.
words.note: From خَمَّنَ, “to guess”.
Also “set, fixed”: مَوْعِدٌ مُحَدَّدٌ.

words.example_meaning_en: I admit that I don't know the answer.
words.note: From اِعْتَرَفَ, “to admit, acknowledge”.

words.example_meaning_en: The teacher explained the term with an example.
words.note: Plural مُصْطَلَحَات.

words.example_meaning_en: In simpler terms, the program protects your account.
words.note: أَبْسَط means “simpler”, from بَسِيط.

words.example_meaning_en: The article was written for specialist readers.
words.note: Also an adjective: مَجَلَّةٌ مُتَخَصِّصَةٌ, “a specialist magazine”.
For a woman: مُبْتَدِئَة. The same root as بَدَأَ, “to begin”.
Present يُبَسِّطُ. The noun تَبْسِيط means “simplification”.

words.example_ar: كَثَافَةُ الْمَعْلُومَاتِ فِي هَذِهِ الْفِقْرَةِ عَالِيَةٌ.
words.example_meaning_en: The density of information in this paragraph is high.
words.note: The adjective is كَثِيف, “dense”.

words.example_meaning_en: Choose a style that suits the reader.
words.note: Plural أَسَالِيب. A formal report and a chat with a friend use different styles.
The adjective is وَاضِح, “clear”.
From تَمَاسَكَ, “to hold together”.
بِطَلَاقَةٍ means “fluently”.

words.example_meaning_en: I care about accuracy and fluency together.
words.note: بِدِقَّةٍ means “precisely”.
Plural مَعَايِير.

words.example_meaning_en: What he said was understandable despite the mistakes.
words.note: Also a noun, “concept”. From فَهِمَ, “to understand”.

words.example_ar: يَحْتَاجُ الْكَاتِبُ إِلَى ثَرْوَةٍ لُغَوِيَّةٍ وَاسِعَةٍ.
words.example_meaning_en: A writer needs a wide range of vocabulary.
words.note: ثَرْوَة alone means “wealth”.

words.example_meaning_en: I understood the point of the story.
words.note: What a text is really getting at.

words.example_meaning_en: There is a long digression in the lecture.
words.note: From اِسْتَطْرَدَ, “to digress”.

words.example_meaning_en: I read the transcript after listening.
words.note: Also “emptying”: تَفْرِيغُ الصُّنْدُوقِ.

words.example_meaning_en: He accepted the idea with some reservation.
words.note: Plural تَحَفُّظَات, “reservations”.

words.example_meaning_en: The text combines narration and description.
words.note: From سَرَدَ, “to narrate”.

words.example_meaning_en: This is the writer's judgement, not a fact.
words.note: Plural أَحْكَام. Also “rule, government”.

words.example_meaning_en: The second part of the text is complicated.
words.note: The opposite: بَسِيط, “simple”.

words.example_meaning_en: She spoke off the cuff about the topic.
words.note: From اِرْتَجَلَ, “to improvise”.

words.example_meaning_en: The topic is familiar, but the question is new.
words.note: From أَلِفَ, “to get used to”. غَيْرُ مَأْلُوفٍ means “unfamiliar”.

words.example_meaning_en: The maximum is four hundred words.
words.note: The minimum: حَدٌّ أَدْنَى.
From تَوَقَّعَ, “to expect”.
عَدَد alone means “number”.

words.example_meaning_en: I wrote a second version of the essay.
words.note: Plural نُسَخ.

words.example_meaning_en: I made a small change to the title.
words.note: Plural تَعْدِيلَات. From عَدَّلَ, “to amend”.
Plural إِنْجَازَات. From أَنْجَزَ, “to accomplish”.

words.example_meaning_en: I chose six samples of my work.
words.note: Plural عَيِّنَات.

words.example_meaning_en: He has a great ability to memorise.
words.note: Plural قُدُرَات. Used with عَلَى.

words.example_meaning_en: The assessor read the text twice.
words.note: For a woman: مُقَيِّمَة. From قَيَّمَ, “to assess”.

words.example_meaning_en: She got a certificate in the language.
words.note: Plural شَهَادَات.

words.example_ar: أَضَفْتُ اللُّغَةَ الْعَرَبِيَّةَ إِلَى سِيرَتِي الذَّاتِيَّةِ.
words.example_meaning_en: I added Arabic to my CV.
words.note: سِيرَة alone means “life story, biography”.
From نَوْع, “kind, type”.

words.example_meaning_en: I asked an independent teacher for an assessment.
words.note: Plural تَقْيِيمَات. From قَيَّمَ, “to assess”.

words.example_meaning_en: I registered for an official exam.
words.note: اِمْتِحَان alone means “exam”. Plural اِمْتِحَانَات.
The singular رَسْم also means “drawing”.
From اِعْتَمَدَ, “to approve; to rely on”.

words.example_ar: أَحْتَاجُ إِلَى تَغْذِيَةٍ رَاجِعَةٍ عَلَى نُطْقِي.
words.example_meaning_en: I need feedback on my pronunciation.
words.note: Also simply مُلَاحَظَات, “comments”.

words.example_ar: أَدْرُسُ مَعَ مُدَرِّسٍ خُصُوصِيٍّ مَرَّةً فِي الْأُسْبُوعِ.
words.example_meaning_en: I study with a private tutor once a week.
words.note: For a woman: مُدَرِّسَةٌ خُصُوصِيَّةٌ.

words.example_meaning_en: Does the assessment include an oral part?
words.note: Also spelled شَفَهِيّ. The opposite is كِتَابِيّ, “written”.
From اِسْتَمَرَّ, “to continue”.

words.example_meaning_en: I chose the field of technology.
words.note: Plural مَجَالَات.

words.example_meaning_en: I keep up my reading every day.
words.note: The noun مُحَافَظَة also means “a province”.
From دَوْرَة, “cycle”.

words.example_meaning_en: I lightened my workload this week.
words.note: عِبْء alone means “burden”.

words.example_ar: عُدْتُ إِلَى الدِّرَاسَةِ بَعْدَ انْقِطَاعٍ طَوِيلٍ.
words.example_meaning_en: I went back to studying after a long break.
words.note: From اِنْقَطَعَ, “to stop, be cut off”.

words.example_ar: أُرِيدُ أَنْ أَقْرَأَ الْأَدَبَ عَلَى الْمَدَى الْبَعِيدِ.
words.example_meaning_en: In the long term I want to read literature.
words.note: In the short term: عَلَى الْمَدَى الْقَرِيبِ.
